title: Special editions: six pieces with something set inside, or air
one_line: Six numbered special editions answering your 31 October idea (things set inside the acrylic, and bubbles), written up with pictures of three. You got the names and a line on each in chat (31 Oct) and captions for the three pictures (1 Nov), but never the pictures themselves or the write-up.
what_was_made: A written proposal (31 October to 1 November): research on earlier work like Miss Blanche, on how to make it and on the law; 18 ideas scored blind by three AI judges (a gallery owner, a brand director, a master acrylic maker); six kept. The work stopped on 1 November and nothing has moved since.

Bubbles. Firn (an edition of 25): flat air bubbles machined into every layer of a clear record weight under a thin Ice-blue top, pressed together warm. Groove (an edition of 33): a spiral air channel tracing the first second of Session 00, sealed in a record weight over a thin Smoke layer. Contour (8 per mountain): the 2,000 m contour line of Mount Shasta drawn as an air channel in a clear wall panel lit from its edge.

Things inside. Iron (12): an etched slice of the Gibeon iron meteorite (about $200 to $400 of metal), treated against rust and sealed dry at the center of a solid clear ball the size of Core, made in two halves, lit from a separate base. Stamper (12 to 16, as many as one stamper yields): a piece of the metal master that pressed the Session 00 record, sealed in a clear record stand.
From the factory. Offcuts (8): a column of clear discs with one thin layer of each of the eight colors, cut from the first eight speakers' leftover sheet, Ember to Smoke, lit from a separate base.

Each is clear acrylic built up in glued layers (no pouring), numbered and signed, with a card saying what is inside and where it came from. Only Firn, Iron and Stamper were pictured, and none passed our picture bar (best 6 out of 10; the bar is 7). No prices (pricing is on hold), only proposed markups, from +70% (Offcuts) to +150-250% (Iron).
out_of_date: Five of the six sit on objects that aren't in the line: the record weight (Moho), record stand (Bedrock) and wall panel (Relief) are the brand team's drafts, which you haven't reviewed, and Offcuts needs a stacked version of Core (Core Sample), a lamps-team proposal you haven't seen, which lost all its picture comparisons and which that team suggests dropping.

The editions team also drew its own versions of those objects, and they don't match the brand team's drafts: its record stand holds one sleeve (the brand team's holds about 80 records), and its record weight is clear, wider and lower, with no brass core.

Written before your 1 November color decision: its color list uses older sheets for every color but Ice, Smoke and Fog among them (it lists a light gray Fog where the line's Fog is now plain clear), and the speakers' Poison and Haze are now lighter custom pours. The three pictures use only clear and Ice, which haven't changed, so they still hold.

Stamper and Groove are made from Session 00, the planned first recording and record, which hasn't happened and was never put to you. Offcuts needs leftover sheet from speakers in all eight colors, but the first pair is planned in gray only.

Iron's lit base doesn't say how it gets power, while Core itself went cordless on the charging dock you signed on 1 November. The only pictures of Iron lit (an earlier dark set, scored 5.0 and 5.5) throw the base's light down onto the floor around it, which breaks your rule, so there is no usable night picture.
The pictures date from 1 November, before the rule that nothing reaches you until a blind critic checks it against your notes, and none passed the old bar either.
needs_from_owner: A look, then one answer: which of the six, if any, to keep working on. Nothing is being made, bought or redrawn until you say.
suggested_pick: Keep Iron and Firn, and set the other four aside until Session 00 and the brand team's new objects are decided.
pick_reason: Iron (a thing set inside) and Firn (bubbles) answer both halves of your idea, have the clearest pictures, and each is settled by a cheap bench test. Iron is the only one built on a product already in the line (Core), and Firn needs only your yes on the record weight; the other four wait on a record not yet made, speakers not yet built, or objects you haven't reviewed.

title: Special editions: three cheap bench tests
one_line: Three small shop tests, planned but never started, that would show whether the editions can really be made: clean designed bubbles, no rust on a sealed meteorite or metal piece, and true colors in thin stacked layers.
what_was_made: Only a written plan (31 October); nothing has been bought, made or quoted, and no test piece exists.

Bubble test: six small squares of clear sheet with machined bubbles, a channel and a spiral, glued two ways, heat-treated, then checked for glue creeping into the bubbles, rings and visible seams, and cycled hot and cold 20 times. It decides how Firn, Groove and Contour are made.

Rust test: an engraved nickel piece and a cheap meteorite end piece (about $40 to $100), each sealed dry with a moisture absorber, kept warm and humid (40 °C, 85%) for 1,000 hours, about six weeks, photographed weekly, then cycled hot and cold. It decides whether Iron can be sold and whether Stamper's grooves stay bright.

Color wedge: eight thin layers, one of each color, glued into one stack; each layer's color and light measured against the sheet maker's chart, and the seams checked. It decides Offcuts and corrects the colors used in the edition pictures.
out_of_date: The color wedge was planned with the older color list. Run now, it would use your 1 November colors: darker stock sheet for most, but Poison and Haze are lighter custom pours that haven't been made yet, so those two layers would have to wait.
It overlaps the color chip check for the whole line, which is also still waiting (about $150 to $200, not bought); the two could be one order.
Any of the three means asking an acrylic shop, and requests to shops are on hold, at your call, until the design settles.
needs_from_owner: Yes or no: may we ask a shop to run these, all three or only the ones for the editions you keep? Nothing has ever been sent to a shop (the quote requests drafted on 31 October are still unsent, on hold at your call), so this would be the first.
suggested_pick: If you keep Iron and Firn, run the rust test and the bubble test, and leave the color wedge until Offcuts comes back.
pick_reason: They are cheap (the meteorite piece is about $40 to $100; the rest is sheet and shop time, not yet quoted) and answer what no picture can: does the meteorite rust, and do the bubbles stay clean. The rust test takes about six weeks, so it should start first; the color wedge mainly serves Offcuts.

title: Planet EARF: the lantern plan
one_line: The bar redesigned as a long, dark room in an ordinary 25 x 80 ft San Francisco storefront, with the listening room built as a freestanding oak box at the back, lit by a glowing band of acrylic fins under the ceiling.
what_was_made: The whole bar redrawn for the size of storefront you're most likely to lease (25 x 80 ft, 2,000 sq ft, apartments above). The shop is at the street, the bar is in the middle, and the listening room is a bolted oak box on its own sprung floor, so the music stays out of the apartments and the box can leave with the lease. Two blind AI critics both picked it over three other ideas.

Seats: 18 in the bar (four stools, two low seats for wheelchair users, four tables along a leather bench) and 18 in the box, with the wheelchair space on the best seat. About 52 people are allowed in all. Inside the box, the Tropos pair faces the door, with Mother EARF standing on a plinth between them.

An estimate of $823k to $1.56M to build ($411 to $779 a sq ft), about a quarter of it for the box. It leaves out the liquor license, the sound system, the products, the furniture and the opening costs. Plus drawings (plan, ceiling, sections, elevations, a cutaway) and four pictures, each through three rounds of critics.

It would replace the 31 Oct business plan's bigger 2,800 sq ft house: 55 seats and about $2.0M to open. That house was close to break-even in a normal year: it needed 87 guests a night with the shop selling EARF pieces, or 114 without the shop.

You were told about it in chat on 31 Oct and given the House Book link, whose lantern page has three of its pictures. It was never shown to you directly or put to you as a decision. No architect, acoustician, engineer or city office has checked it.

The globe in the lantern pictures is the six-color one, which you chose for the bar on the evening of 22 October (your notes now record it). Whether she keeps six colors is the question on the Mother EARF look card.

The House Book is behind. Its cover picture and top numbers still describe the older 2,800 sq ft house (55 seats, $2.0M). Its lantern page is the first version (20 seats, a 3 ft back wall with a bench in it) with the earlier pictures. It calls the band amber, but the design notes say Smoke and leave the color open. Its night-by-night section still describes the older house (a zinc counter, the globe hanging over a long table, the coin column). It calls the coin price "quoted" when no shop was asked.
The money plan (cost to open, break-even) was worked out for the 2,800 sq ft, 55-seat house. It hasn't been redone for the lantern's 36 seats.
The cutaway drawing still shows the first layout, with the small entry porch beside the box. The plan has since moved the porch in line with the box and shortened the counter.
The lantern keeps almost none of the acrylic you asked for in the bar (see the card on the dropped pieces).

It also drops the second Tropos pair you chose for the bar on 20 October, raised on ledges at counter height beside the decks. The only pair is inside the box, so the bar room itself has no EARF speaker.

title: Planet EARF: the road to opening
one_line: The researched path from a debut night to two pop-up shops to the full bar, with the liquor license route, candidate sites, and a drafted application to the city's empty-storefront program that was never sent.
what_was_made: Three steps, each paid for by the one before, after a debut night: an 8-week pop-up in a downtown storefront ($22k to $36k), then a 5-month pop-up ($130k to $210k, roughly paying for itself at six Tropos pairs sold), then the full bar (about $2.0M).

The license route: buy an existing full liquor license from another bar (about $100,000) and add a city permit for a DJ. That takes about 8 months from a signed lease, or 11 to 12 months where the zoning needs a special city approval (a Conditional Use). In the pop-ups EARF never sells alcohol: a partner bar pours on its own catering permit ($100 a night, at most 36 nights a year at one address).

Sites. For the full bar: Folsom Street in SoMa (1539 Folsom, a former bar at $27.25 a sq ft a year, its building for sale) or a smaller Hayes Valley space, with Oakland as the cheap fallback. For the pop-up: eight downtown storefronts ranked, with 311 Grant and 333 O'Farrell first and 570 Market for a short lease. Spring debut rooms are ranked too, Gray Area's theater first.

A drafted application to Vacant to Vibrant, the city program that places pop-ups in empty downtown storefronts for three months with a $2,000 to $10,000 grant. The rent was free in 2023, but the program's current pages no longer say so. It is unsent, with blanks only you can fill.
All of it comes from public web pages read on 31 Oct. Nobody was contacted, and nothing was applied for or signed.
out_of_date: On 31 Oct you moved the debut to spring, then parked dates and logistics to focus on design. The January plan (Fort Mason during FOG week, a Park Police permit by 8 December, the debut on Tuesday 19 January) is stale, but the House Book still shows it as the timeline, and the pop-up plan still assumes February to April 2027.

EARF isn't a registered business yet. The program's pages don't say an applicant must be one, but the team expects a grant, a lease and the first sale to need one. Registering takes about three weeks. On 31 October you chose to wait on a company until the first money comes in.

The costs, the break-even and the sites were worked out for the 2,800 sq ft house and the 25 x 50 ft pop-up. Nothing was searched at the lantern's 25 x 80 ft size; the nearest storefronts on the list are 564 Market and 311 Grant.

title: Names held in reserve
one_line: Three product names the Brand Book has held for later since 31 October: Crust, Strata and Ozone.
what_was_made: Three names kept in reserve in the Book’s naming chapter, in the same “layers of the Earth” family as Tropos and Mantle: Crust, Strata and Ozone, for a stand, a rack and something that moves air.
Each was to wait for your yes and a trademark search before use. No search has been done.
out_of_date: Strata clashes twice. Designer Fernando Mastrangelo already uses “Strata” for his layered pieces: the brand team’s own rules say to stay clear of it, and its new floor lamp was renamed Lithos for that reason. Inside EARF, “Strata” already names the stepped Tropos design and Mantle’s chosen design, Strata Float.
The stepped horn that suggested the name has been replaced by horn A, and the Book now keeps Strata “as a name only”.
The new objects already propose Bedrock for a record stand, the kind of product these names were held for.
needs_from_owner: Yes, no or other names for the three, before anyone pays for a trademark search.
suggested_pick: Drop Strata as a product name, and keep Crust and Ozone in reserve, unsearched, until a product needs one.
pick_reason: Strata is already another designer’s name for the same kind of layered object and already labels two EARF designs, so as a product name it would confuse people and may not be ours to register. Holding the other two costs nothing until they’re needed.

title: Seven big ideas
one_line: Seven ranked ideas to raise the odds of funding and sales, each with a mockup and a short plan, from the Founding Hundred to Mother EARF as public art.
what_was_made: Seven plans, each with a mockup picture and a short plan, ranked by what each does for the odds per dollar. Every cost is an estimate, and nobody has been contacted.

1 The Founding Hundred: the first hundred pairs reserved and numbered on their plates · 2 The Tint Library: the eight colors as tiles in a birch tray, a trade sample kit · 3 EARF Sessions: live albums recorded in the listening room and pressed in the night’s color.

4 Hotel listening suites fitted by EARF · 5 A debut room: San Francisco, then High End Vienna (May 2027), then Milan (2028) · 6 Artist editions: a ninth color made once a year with an artist · 7 Mother EARF as public art: the globe at 4 m for a plaza.
This morning the plans’ dates were changed to count from the debut. The mockups were not redrawn.
EARF Sessions has since become a full plan, Session 00 (the format, eight artists, the recording, the rights, pressing quotes and a budget); it was never put to you.
out_of_date: The debut-room mockup still says “San Francisco · January 2027”.
The Sessions record jacket and the artist-edition picture show the October Tropos (horn on posts), and the jacket’s pair stands on lit plinths.
The Tint Library tiles were rendered on 31 October, before the darker November colors.
The public-art drawing shows the globe’s colors pooled on the paving below it, which may clash with your rule that light glows through the acrylic rather than down onto the ground.
needs_from_owner: Which idea to pursue first, or none for now.
suggested_pick: Start with the Tint Library (see its own card for the drawn, costed version), and keep the Founding Hundred ready for when a first pair can be heard.
pick_reason: It fits your focus on getting the design and colors real. A kit costs about $100 to $250, needs no dates or lawyers, and puts the true colors in people’s hands as soon as the sheets are chosen. The Founding Hundred, ranked first for money, needs counsel and a pair to hear before anyone can reserve.

title: Packaging
one_line: How Tropos and the lamps arrive: an upright crate whose door lowers into a ramp, a separate horn case, and lamp boxes dyed in each color.
what_was_made: Tropos ships upright in a birch crate whose front door is hinged at the foot and lowers to the floor as a ramp, so two people walk the speaker out on a sled with felt runners. The steps are printed inside the door, and a dyed cotton sleeve stays on as its dust cover.
Both horns travel face up in a separate case. Each Hemisphere shade comes in a drum of board dyed its color, and Core comes in a dyed cube.
Three renders (the closed crates, the open crate and the lamp boxes) and the printed faces. Sizes and tests are proposals, and nothing has been quoted.
out_of_date: The crate pictures print “about 74 kg”; the plan now says 72.6 kg.
The horn case is still sized for the older, wider horn (635 mm). Horn A sits flush with the cabinet at 560 mm.
The open crate holds the 1 November speaker with its horn off. Whether the lit plinth ships in its own carton is undecided, since you reopened the base on 3 November.

The crate renders scored 5.5 of 10 with a blind critic on 31 October and stopped there, because made-up wood and cloth look fake. The current versions were re-rendered on 1 November without a new score, and the lamp boxes were never scored.
needs_from_owner: A yes or no on the idea (the door as a ramp, a separate horn case, dyed boxes). The sizes wait for the final speaker and a crate maker’s quote.
suggested_pick: Approve the idea, stop rendering it, and get a crate maker’s quote once the speaker’s size and base are settled. Photograph the first real crate rather than rendering it again.
pick_reason: Three tries couldn’t lift the renders past 5.5 because the wood and cloth are made up, and the brand team concluded a photo of the first real crate will sell it better. The crate can’t be sized until the base question is answered.
